articles.title: Ed Davey takes aim at Reform and Elon Musk as Lib Dem conference begins
articles.summary:
Leader says party ‘won’t give up the fight’ to defeat ‘nasty populism’ in first-day speech to delegates

The Liberal Democrats’ leader, Sir Ed Davey, took aim at Nigel Farage’s Reform UK and…

blocks.text: The Liberal Democrats’ leader, Sir Ed Davey, took aim at Nigel Farage’s Reform UK and Elon Musk on the first day of his party’s annual conference, saying that they “won’t give up the fight” to defeat “nasty populism” and the far-right party’s “£72m arsenal of hate and lies”.

Speaking from the main stage at Brighton Centre, Davey called on the assembled delegates not to be deterred in the face of Reform’s hope “that the anger and the hatred and the lies will grind us down until eventually we just give up”, and praised earlier speakers for showing “why we care and why we fight”.
He contrasted this with Reform, which “care about their own bank balance and they fight because two crypto billionaires gave them 72m quid”.

Davey, who entered conference season having to address frustrations over his leadership expressed by some Lib Dem MPs, also used the speech to recall his early political life as a student campaigning successfully for his university college to boycott Barclays, due to its investments in apartheid-era South Africa.

He spoke of his “visceral shock [and] overwhelming anger at seeing human beings treating other human beings with total contempt” and drew parallels between that experience and the need to not look away “when we see human dignity under attack”.

Davey said: “Today – we are back. Fighting again the fight that fired me up at university. The fight to end injustices. In our country and around the world. The fight to defeat the nasty populism of Trump, Le Pen, the AfD and the rest.
“The fight to stop the world’s richest man who learned racism in apartheid South Africa from funding racism around the world.”

Referring to recent abuse from far-right agitators aimed at the RNLI, Davey also pointed to the “fight to defend the Royal National Lifeboat Institution after volunteers for the coastal rescue charity were recently targeted online amid anti-migrant protests”.

He said that “Reform know they don’t speak for the real United Kingdom” and what Farage was “counting on to get him to No 10” was that people would get “tired, depressed, fed up of seeing Zia Yusuf on BBC Question Time week after week”.
But Davey said he hoped Reform were watching and would see “a party that won’t be ground down. That won’t be deterred. That won’t give up the fight”.

Also during the first day of the conference, Lib Dem health spokesperson Helen Morgan set out a £600m plan to improve maternity care, including proposals to bring in one-to-one midwifery for every woman in labour backed by a round-the-clock senior consultant.
The party said the measures will pay for themselves by reducing how much the NHS has to spend on compensation for maternity negligence claims every year – totalling £1.3bn in 2024-25.

Munira Wilson, the Lib Dem education spokesperson, said the party would introduce a guarantee to provide 100 hours of work experience for students from GCSE age to 18 to tackle the crisis of young people not in education, employment or training.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia confirms Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia on Saturday confirmed that Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile, the first targeting of Riyadh since the escalation in fighting with the…

image.caption: A large plume of black smoke rises from the fuel storage area at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday. (Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Saudi Arabia on Saturday confirmed that Yemen's Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile, the first targeting of Riyadh since the escalation in fighting with the Tehran-backed rebels that has opened a new front in the Iran war.
Attempted attack comes amid escalation in fighting between Saudis and Houthis

The statement by the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis came long after the dawn attempt, which the coalition said was intercepted. Some residents in Riyadh heard an explosion. Later, some saw a plume of smoke near the airport. There were no reports of casualties or damage.

The statement also said the Houthis tried to attack civilian infrastructure in the Red Sea port city of Yanbu — where a key Saudi pipeline ends — and in Taif, Baysh and Farasan but they were thwarted, giving no further details.

The Houthis earlier claimed, without providing evidence, that they had targeted "sensitive sites" in Riyadh and facilities of Saudi oil giant Aramco in Yanbu, causing "massive fires." Aramco, the world's largest oil company, did not respond to a request for comment.

items: Houthis attack more Saudi targets as regional talks with Iran postponed
Saudis pound Yemen as Houthis solidify gains in new Middle East war front

blocks.text: The growing conflict near another important global shipping corridor has brought new pressures for markets.

Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree claimed they attacked with cruise and ballistic missiles as well as drones. He said Saudi Arabia had attempted to target the rebel-held city of Sanaa in neighbouring Yemen, without giving details. The Associated Press couldn't independently verify the claims.
Escalating conflict

Recent days have seen one escalation after another. On Thursday, the first civilian casualty was reported as the Saudi civil defence said debris from an intercepted Houthi drone killed a Yemeni resident of Saudi Arabia.

And on Wednesday, Saudi Arabia said the Houthis had tried to attack Mecca, Islam's holiest city, with a drone that it said was intercepted, calling the security of the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad a "red line." The Houthis fiercely denied the accusation.
CBC News Network speaks to Charles Kupchan on the recent escalation between the Houthis and Saudis

The United States, a close Saudi ally, has signalled it has no current fight with the Houthis. Regional officials have told The Associated Press that Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and instead has asked France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt for air defence support.

Meanwhile, fighting has surged inside Yemen between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government. The rebels raced down the country's Red Sea coast over a week ago, seizing the key port city of Mokha and islands on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.
That has improved their surveillance of passing ships, though the Houthis have said they are only targeting Saudi ones.
The fighting in Yemen also marks a return to a devastating civil war after four years of relative calm.

articles.title: US, Canada slam ‘deliberate ramming’ by Chinese vessel
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The United States and Canada affirmed the Philippines’ position on Friday’s attack on one of its vessels, with both countries calling that incident a “deliberate ramming” by the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The United States and Canada affirmed the Philippines’ position on Friday’s attack on one of its vessels, with both countries calling that incident a “deliberate ramming” by the China Coast Guard (CCG).

US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton on Friday said on X (formerly twitter): “We STRONGLY CONDEMN the China Coast Guard’s DELIBERATE RAMMING of the Philippine BFAR (Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources) vessel near Bombay Shoal, just 54 [nautical miles] off the coast of Palawan.”
Lipton also commended the “sustained professionalism” of the Philippines in response to that attack.
‘Illegal, coercive’

The Canadian Embassy on Saturday said on Facebook: “Canada is concerned by the Chinese Coast Guard deliberately ramming into a Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources fisheries enforcement vessel off the coast of the Philippines.”
“These dangerous maneuvers jeopardize regional peace and stability,” it added.
The BFAR vessel was delivering fuel assistance to Filipino fishermen in the West Philippine Sea when it was struck by CCG-21585 about 100 kilometers (54 nautical miles) from the coast of Palawan.

Rear Adm. Jay Tarriela, PCG spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea, said Friday that CCG-21585 had “intentionally” rammed the Datu Magat Salamat, calling it “the closest ever that China Coast Guard did this intentional ramming and disregarded the safety of our personnel,”

No Coast Guard or BFAR personnel were injured. But the collision damaged the BFAR vessel’s railings, deck, stanchions and other structures, forcing it to cut short its mission to deliver subsidized fuel to Filipino fishermen.

China Coast Guard spokesperson Jiang Lue said the Philippine vessel ignored repeated warnings before deliberately changing course and accelerating across the bow of the Chinese ship. He said the Philippine side was responsible for the incident.

The National Maritime Council on Saturday said it was “particularly concerned that the illegal, coercive, aggressive and dangerous actions of the CCG vessel placed the civilian crew of the BFAR vessel at unnecessary risk while carrying out a legitimate livelihood-support mission.” INQ

articles.title: Trump says US will form 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar
articles.summary: The president said his administration "will not in any way hinder or stifle the growth" amid amid warnings about the emergent technology.

blocks.text: Claims by current and former researchers that the tech will endanger humanity - with one suggesting there is a greater than 10% chance of it "killing all humans" - have raised alarm bells in recent weeks.
Major AI companies have been racing to develop better systems, including creating what they call super intelligence - theoretical tech which is smarter than humans.

AI titans Anthropic, OpenAI and Google - the tech companies behind Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, respectively - have also disclosed instances of security breaches or incidents in which their chatbots were used for "malicious activity".
Anthropic head Dario Amodei recently called for AI development to slow down and proposed industry-wide deceleration and regulation, as well as independent monitoring of AI model development.
Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk of xAI have both said they agree with his recommendations.
Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, told BBC that a "kill switch" that can be checked by a third party may need to be mandatory for the industry.

The warnings have prompted US lawmakers to propose legislation around the technology but Altman suggested this week that Washington has struggled to keep pace with the new tech and how to regulate it. He said people should have more faith in AI firms to keep it safe.
"The world should trust that we are going to do the right thing because it's the right thing and we feel the magnitude of this," Altman told a conference in San Francisco.

In the UK, MPs across parties and peers have identified human rights risks posed by artificial intelligence and have argued that existing laws are ill-equipped to address the technology's rapid growth.
The Joint Committee on Human Rights (JCHR) has published a report calling for a new bill on AI to "address the scale and seriousness" of such threats.

articles.title: Israeli president pardons combat medic who shot dead wounded Palestinian attacker
articles.summary:
Elor Azaria’s conviction in 2017 for manslaughter of man who stabbed soldier continues to divide country

Israel’s president has pardoned a combat medic who shot dead a badly wounded…

blocks.text: Israel’s president has pardoned a combat medic who shot dead a badly wounded Palestinian attacker who had stabbed a soldier in the occupied West Bank, in a case that divided the country a decade ago.

Elor Azaria’s conviction in 2017 for manslaughter and his release after serving two-thirds of his 18-month sentence drew enormous attention in Israel, where military service is compulsory for most Jewish men.
In his first interview after his release, Azaria said he would “act exactly the same, because that’s how I needed to act”.

Azaria had approached Abdel Fattah al-Sharif as he lay on the ground, unarmed and badly hurt, after stabbing a soldier in the city of Hebron. A mobile phone video captured Azaria shooting al-Sharif in the head.

The office of president Isaac Herzog said in a statement on Saturday that he acted on the recommendation of defence minister Israel Katz. The statement cited the time that had passed, and the spirit of the approaching Yom Kippur, or Day of Atonement, holiday as among the factors in the decision.

Herzog’s office also said that Azaria, who was 20 when he was sentenced, had “expressed his sorrow” in his request. The statement noted that in an earlier request, he called his gunshot an “operational error”.
In a separate statement, Katz called it a “right, humane and fitting decision” and said Azaria had been in a “complex operational mission”.
But the military’s chief of staff, Lt Gen Eyal Zamir, had said in a letter to the defence minister that the pardon should not be granted, Israeli media reported.

The conviction was a rare case of a military court ruling against a soldier for deadly action taken in the field. Top generals had pressed for his prosecution, while many in the Israeli public supported Azaria at a time when there had been a series of stabbings and car-ramming attacks by Palestinians or Israeli Arabs. Some supporters protested outside his trial.

On Saturday, Israel’s hard-line national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said in a statement that “cancelling the criminal record of someone who killed a terrorist makes me emotional and very happy”.
Some Palestinians and human rights groups had described Azaria’s sentence as far too lenient. Prosecutors had sought a sentence of three to five years.
The statement by Herzog’s office on Saturday said that his decision “does not constitute a reassessment of the case”.
The divisions over Azaria’s case led to public polling and political pressure that led the defence minister at the time, Moshe Ya’alon, to resign.
After the verdict, Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for Azaria to be pardoned.
After the sentencing, the Palestinian government minister in charge of prisoner affairs, Issa Karaka, called it a “joke”.

articles.title: As tobacconist firebombings intensify in Melbourne, nearby stores are being denied insurance
articles.summary:
Arson attacks related to illegal tobacco trade are also causing revenue and reputation problems for neighbouring businesses

  • Get our

blocks.text: Small businesses located near tobacconists are being denied insurance or priced out of coverage as rising arson attacks turn neighbouring shops into collateral damage.

The problem has intensified after a spate of firebombings, which includes a recent Melbourne blaze that destroyed a Richmond tobacco retailer and nearly a dozen neighbouring shops, requiring 80 firefighters to contain.

Crime syndicates have been implicated in more than 200 firebombings of commercial and residential premises in Australia since 2023, according to government data, as rival groups vie for control of the illicit tobacco market.
A Melbourne retailer, who asked not to be identified, told Guardian Australia their insurer refused to renew a policy because they were a “few doors down” from a tobacconist.
“Even if we re-located, which is not really an option for us, who’s to say a tobacconist doesn’t move in next door?” the retailer said.
The retailer said they’d received quotes from other insurers that don’t include fire cover.
Legitimate tobacconists have also reportedly been targeted by syndicates expanding their revenue base, making it difficult for them to secure coverage as well.
Skye Cappuccio, the chief executive of the Council of Small Business Organisations Australia, said accessing or affording insurance for businesses located near tobacconists was becoming problematic.
“Small businesses should not be left carrying the financial consequences of criminal activity that is beyond their control,” Cappuccio said.

“We need a comprehensive effort from governments, law enforcement and regulators to address the illicit tobacco market, alongside broader action to address rising insurance costs and access to affordable cover for small businesses.”
Small businesses close to tobacco market-related firebombings are also affected by loss of foot traffic, revenue and reputation, according to the Australian Criminal Intelligence Commission.

While insurers have not disclosed what constitutes “close proximity”, brokers generally consider it to be within about 20 metres of a tobacconist. Tobacco retailers within shopping complexes are seen as a lower risk.

Illicit tobacco accounted for 80% of the cigarettes smoked by Australians in 2025, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, with untaxed packets costing as little as $10 compared with more than $40 for a legal packet.
after newsletter promotion

The surge in demand has sparked a political debate over whether Australia should reduce the tobacco excise to make legal cigarettes cheaper in order to curb illegal sales. Health experts have called for a focus on enforcement, which includes intercepting illegal products that enter the country through Australia’s ports.
A spokesperson at Suncorp said the insurer no longer offered insurance cover for tobacconist retailers, including renewals for existing customers.

The representative said businesses located near tobacconists may still be eligible, with underwriting decisions based on a range of factors, including the nature of the business and location-specific risks.
“As with all commercial insurance, applications are considered on a case-by-case basis,” the spokesperson said.
A QBE spokesperson said decisions were assessed individually.
“Where risk profiles change, this can influence the price, terms or availability of cover,” the spokesperson said.

articles.title: Trump to create ‘AI Force’ to monitor technology as fears over out-of-control agents grow
articles.summary:
President had brushed away suggestions to slow down AI technology, even as his own party counseled caution

Donald Trump on…

blocks.text: Donald Trump on Saturday said he would appoint an artificial intelligence czar and create an “AI Force” to help monitor the technology, though he gave almost no details about either plan.

As global fears over AI have grown, especially in the past week in the face of multiple industry figures sounding the alarm about its dangers, the president has been critical of calls to slow down development of the fast-moving industry.

The creation of a czar and a new AI body in the US appears a response to critics of his stance, which in part is born out of a fear that China will best the US in AI development if the industry in America does not continue its rapid growth. However, even many Republicans have been calling for caution and an AI slowdown in the face of its potential threat to public safety.

“I am forming the AI Force, much like I did Space Force, which has been a tremendous SUCCESS, in my First Term. To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI ‘Czar’ – Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!” Trump said in a social media post.
But in the post, Trump also repeated his stance that the rapidly emerging technology – which some industry experts fear poses a threat to human existence – is being unfairly maligned.
Trump called the fears surrounding AI a “hoax”.

“Over the years, there have been many Hoaxes, all generated by the Radical Left Dumocrats, for purposes of destroying our Country,” he fulminated, including in a list of grievances Russian interference in the 2016 election, Ukraine, global warming, two impeachments, men in women’s sports and “transgender for everyone”.

The latest, he wrote, is “the decimation, or destruction, of AI, commonly known as Artificial Intelligence”, and vowed that his administration “will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry”.

The president said that any “bad actors” in AI industry could be addressed by criminal and civil systems of justice. “AI is the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger and more impactful, possibly as much as 25% of our Country’s GDP,” Trump predicted, concluding that the US is “leading China, and the rest of the World, and I intend to keep it that way”.

The post came after an earlier missive in which he questioned the term “artificial intelligence” – coined by American computer scientist John McCarthy in 1955 and defined as the capability of computer systems or algorithms to imitate intelligent human behavior – to describe the accelerating data-processing revolution now under way.
Trump said that “a far more elegant and accurate description of this new phenomena would be Superior Intelligence (SI) or, Extreme Intelligence (EI) or, Supreme Intelligence (SI)”.

Trump’s proposal comes ahead of his meeting with the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, next Thursday as the UN general assembly takes place in New York. The US and China are competing for leadership ⁠in the AI sector.

The announcement of a planned AI czar also came a day after California’s governor, Gavin Newsom, announced plans for a panel to develop safety regulations for state’s AI companies that would include the development of a possible “kill switch” for AI programs that become misaligned, or go rogue, from human programmers.
after newsletter promotion

As recently as Monday, Trump argued on social media that his administration had done enough to prevent risks of catastrophe. He described calls to slow AI development as part of a “SICK conspiracy” to benefit China.
“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades,” he wrote.

Ahead of the midterm elections, politicians from both political parties are scrambling to find a path to support tech innovation while responding to rising public and industry fears of technological change.

The frenzy kicked off earlier this month when a young researcher who had been employed at the AI company Anthropic said AI companies are “gambling with our lives” and even “people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade”.

AI executives, including Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Dario Amodei have since called for a slowdown in the technology’s growth in the wake of an incident in which a swarm of AI agents created by OpenAI acted as a “fanatically devoted collective conducting cybersecurity attacks on targets they were not asked to attack”.
Trump’s call for an AI czar comes after many Republicans have rejected his hands-off approach.

Florida’s governor, Ron DeSantis, has advocated for AI controls, and that state’s attorney general, James Uthmeier, has called for laws allowing the state to criminally charge companies for illegal acts carried out with the use of their technologies. Utah’s Republican governor, Spencer Cox, has called on Congress to pass AI safety laws and block the sale of high-end technology to China.

articles.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
articles.summary: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.

image.caption: Older people are more vulnerable to extreme heat Image: Joel Saget/AFP

blocks.text: The summer (June to August) of 2026 was the warmest in Europe since records began, beating the record set in 2003, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service,

Not only that, Germany's DWD weather service says that there was an "unprecedented" number of hot days this year. "On average across Germany,there were about 22 hot days with temperatures of at least 30 degrees Celsius and about five very hot days with temperatures of at least 35 degrees Celsius," the DWD wrote in in a press release at the end of August.

The estimated number of heat-related deaths also reached unprecedented levels, with at least 16,300 people dying by the end of August, even if few of them died directly because of the heat, but rather as a consequence of underlying health conditions exacerbated by the heat.

The figures were compiled from a statistical correlation between the number of deaths recorded by Germany's Federal Statistical Office and the temperatures measured by the DWD during a specific period.

Heat-related deaths in Germany are more likely if the average weekly temperature reaches 20 degrees Celsius or more. This is the average of all hourly temperatures recorded in a week, including at nighttime.

This year, the average weekly temperatures in the country rose above the 20-degree mark several times. It was particularly hot at the end of June, when the average weekly temperature reached above 26 degrees between the 22nd and 28th of the month.
Why Europe's extreme summers are getting worse
Excess mortality during heat waves

Though it is not possible to determine a cause of death using statistics, researchers and medical professionals have a good understanding of how heat affects the human body, and there is widespread consensus that excess mortality during heat waves is possible.

"It was not just the high temperatures on the thermometer that were important, but also how long the heat lasted and the fact that it hardly cooled down at night," said Andreas Matzarakis, professor of environmental meteorology at Freiburg University.
Many people have trouble sleeping on hot nights. Yet, getting enough sleep is important so that the body can recover from the heat and stress of the day.

Matzarakis said that the severity of heat stress was not related solely to air temperatures. Humidity, solar radiation and wind also played a role — and what is known as the 'felt' temperature. He said that humidity and still air could place a heavy strain on the body, even in moderate temperatures.
Powerful El Nino set to bring extreme weather
Underprivileged most vulnerable

The less privileged members of society were also among the most vulnerable, said Martin Röösli, environmental scientist at the Swiss Tropical and Public Health Institute in Basel. "They are more likely to live in homes that are not well insulated or are more likely to work outdoors."

A large proportion of those who died because of the heat probably had only a short life expectancy left, due to their age and medical conditions, but Röösli said that there was a consensus that "some of the deceased could have lived for a long time and were simply in a fragile state at the time of the heat wave."

For Alexandra Schneider, a meteorologist and epidemiologist at the Helmholtz center in Munich in southern Germany, the deaths that occurred during the heat waves were very likely not only because of the "harvesting effect," which describes "how a heat wave causes very vulnerable individuals in particular to die a few days or weeks prematurely."

Had this been the case, there would have been a deficit of mortality in the following weeks, which did not happen. Thus, she believes, a significant proportion of those who died could have lived on for months or even years.
This article was translated from German.

articles.title: Dutch riot police break up violent far-right protest in The Hague
articles.summary:
Authorities ban anti-immigration march after fireworks and other projectiles thrown at officers in city centre park

Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred

blocks.text: Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred far-right protesters in The Hague on Saturday after violence erupted and local authorities banned a planned march in the city against immigration and asylum policies.
The Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported that 24 people had been arrested, after some protesters threw fireworks and other projectiles at police.
Justice minister David van Weel called on X for an “extremely firm” response to what he described as “disgusting scenes” at the protest, organised by the far-right We Are the People organisation.
He said demonstrators made Nazi salutes, chanted antisemitic slogans, and attacked and threw fireworks at police.
“Thanks to all the police officers who are once again standing up for our democratic rule of law,” he wrote.

blocks.caption: The march was organised to protest about immigration and asylum policies in the Netherlands. Photograph: James Petermeier/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The Hague municipality banned the march after violence broke out among demonstrators gathered at the Malieveld, a park in the city centre, and later ordered the crowd to disperse.
Those arrested were detained for various offences, including failing to comply with the order and illegally possessing weapons.
Police reportedly used pepper spray and a water cannon on the rioters.
Saturday’s unrest came a year after rioting erupted during a rightwing demonstration in The Hague.

A police car was set on fire during the clashes between black-clad protesters and police. The headquarters of the centrist D66 party – whose leader, Rob Jetten, is now prime minister – was also attacked.
Jetten said on X that the demonstrators deliberately sought confrontation with the police and chanted “abhorrent” far-right and antisemitic slogans.

articles.title: 2 killed in plane crash during night flight near Kisbey, Sask.
articles.summary: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada and the RCMP are investigating a plane crash near Kisbey, Sask. Harv's Air, the flight school the plane was registered to, confirmed both people on board…

image.caption: This Cessna 172 plane registered to Harv's Air, a flight school based in St. Andrews, Man., crashed near Kisbey, Sask., early on Sept. 18. (Harv's Air)

blocks.text: Saskatchewan

The Transportation Safety Board of Canada and the RCMP are investigating a plane crash near Kisbey, Sask. Harv's Air, the flight school the plane was registered to, confirmed both people on board died in the crash.
Transportation Safety Board of Canada and RCMP investigating
Two people are dead after a Cessna 172 plane crashed near Kisbey, Sask., according to a statement from Adam Penner, the president of Harv's Air, the flight school the plane was registered to.
According to the statement, two people were on board the flight from Regina to Steinbach, Man., via Carlyle, Sask., on a night cross country flight early Friday morning.
Both people in the plane were licensed pilots who rented the plane to gain time toward their commercial pilot licences, Penner said in an email to CBC.
The plane was reported to the Transportation Safety Board of Canada as overdue to arrive at 10:30 a.m. CDT.
According to Lieutenant Zoë Hollander, a public affairs officer for the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre, Trenton, the JRCC led and coordinated the response to the overdue aircraft.
"A CC 138 Hercules from 435 squadron successfully located the crash site, and then inserted search and rescue technicians by parachute," Hollander said.
She said after the search and rescue was complete, the JRCC transferred the case to RCMP.
The statement from Penner said the plane was located by search and rescue at approximately 6 p.m. CDT and both occupants were found dead at the scene.

"The entire Harv's Air family is shocked and saddened by this tragedy. Both pilots had close ties to their fellow students and instructors. We extend our deepest condolences to family and friends," Penner said in the statement.
This is the third incident involving the St. Andrews, Man., based flight school since January 2025.
An instructor employed by Harv's Air was struck by the propeller of a small aircraft as a student attempted to start its engine and was seriously injured in January 2025.
In July 2025, two student pilots were killed when their single engine planes collided mid-air during a training exercise.
The Transportation Safety Board of Canada, along with Transport Canada and the RCMP are working with Harv's Air to determine the cause of the crash according to the release.

articles.title: Victorian Labor promises new offences to close domestic and family violence ‘loopholes’
articles.summary:
Premier Ben Carroll vows to legislate new form of manslaughter and increase maximum penalty for rape to life imprisonment

  • Get our

blocks.text: A re-elected Victorian Labor government will create two new Australian-first offences aimed at closing “loopholes” it says have allowed perpetrators of family violence to escape punishment.

On Sunday, the premier, Ben Carroll, will announce an election commitment to legislate a new form of manslaughter covering cases in which a person takes their own life as a result of family violence, as well as a new offence covering perpetrators abandoning a victim in need of medical care.
The latter responds to recommendations made by the coroner after the deaths of Belinda Jones and Narelle Simmons.

Jones, 40, died on the floor of her Maryborough home in July 2023 after her partner left her there overnight and then waited two hours to call an ambulance after waking to find her cold and not breathing.

Jones had succumbed to treatable bacterial infections and sepsis, which a hospital failed to diagnose during an emergency presentation days earlier. Her partner was not charged with any offence in relation to her death.

In her findings published last month, the state coroner, Liberty Sanger, said: “In my view, the act of abandoning a victim of family violence requiring medical attention is an act of family violence, that instils fear in the victim and affirms a perpetrator’s control over the victim.”
Simmons, 42, died in October 2021 after her partner admitted to punching her twice in the face and elbowing her once in the back of the head before leaving her Cranbourne home.
Her body was found nine days later after her daughter requested a welfare check. Sanger was unable to determine whether she died immediately after the assault or hours or days later.

Her partner – whom the coroner said had 18 previous family violence victims – pleaded guilty to common assault and failing to report a reportable death. He was sentenced to five months’ imprisonment and a 12-month community corrections order.
The government’s media release said the two new offences would close “loopholes” that allow perpetrators to “slip through the cracks in the justice system and walk free”.

The government has also committed to increasing the maximum penalty for rape from 25 years to life imprisonment and upping the maximum penalty for every other serious sexual offence by five years. The maximum penalty for persistent breaches of family violence intervention orders would also double from five years’ imprisonment to 10.
It will also make the standard sentence for the murder of a current or former partner 30 years – up from 25.
after newsletter promotion

Labor will amend the Evidence Act to prevent barristers from using humiliating and invasive questioning techniques on victim-survivors in court. Courts would also be able to consider patterns of sexual abuse as evidence at trial.

The announcement follows a week of crime-focused election commitments from Carroll, including creating a new police training facility in Melbourne’s western suburbs and the introduction of Jack’s Law, which would give police and protective services officers the power to stop and search people for knives using handheld metal detectors.
“I’m a tough-on-crime premier – and that means being tough on family and sexual violence,” Carroll said in a statement ahead of Sunday’s announcement.
“We must act on the violence that is killing a Victorian woman every two weeks.”

The Coalition last year committed to Jack’s Law and also have plans to expand adult sentencing for youth offenders, increase police numbers and split the existing court of appeal into two separate entities, if elected in November.

articles.title: California warns of measles exposure in six counties from unvaccinated train passenger
articles.summary:
Health authorities work to notify people who were exposed to person who traveled through at least six counties

California public…

blocks.text: California public health officials are warning of a possible measles exposure spanning multiple counties after an infected and unvaccinated passenger traveled through the state via Amtrak trains and thruway buses.
The warning comes as the US faces its largest measles resurgence in more than three decades, fueled largely by growing vaccine hesitancy.
The California department of public health said the traveler passed through at least six counties – Alameda, Butte, Kern, Los Angeles, Sacramento and San Joaquin – while making multiple transfers.

Officials said the passenger entered California on an Amtrak train that arrived in Los Angeles on 10 September. From there, the traveler continued to Bakersfield before heading through Stockton, Oroville, Sacramento and Emeryville, eventually leaving California for Denver.
Health officials said passengers who were onboard the same trains or buses, as well as people who were inside the stations along the route on the dates involved, have been exposed to measles.
The state said it is working with federal partners and local health departments to identify and notify people who may have been exposed.

“This case, along with previous measles outbreaks in California this year, serve as reminders of the importance of vaccination against measles,” assistant state public health officer Rita Nguyen said in a statement. “The measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine is safe and provides long-lasting protection against measles. Vaccination protects both our own families and those who are too young to be fully vaccinated.”

Pennsylvania is currently dealing with the country’s worst active measles outbreak. The Pennsylvania health department announced on Wednesday that 731 cases have been confirmed across 38 counties so far this year. At least four people in the state have died from measles-related illness.

Pennsylvania is now seeking emergency assistance from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) as the outbreak continues to spread. State officials have warned, however, that the request could be withdrawn unless the CDC publicly recognizes the four measles-associated deaths, something the US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, previously instructed the CDC not to do.

And as the death toll from the outbreak continues to rise, Kennedy headlined the Washington DC conference of the anti-vaccine organization Children’s Health Defense earlier this week, an group he led for nearly a decade.

He only addressed the measles outbreak in Pennsylvania once during his speech, instead peddling unfounded fears about vaccines at a time when health experts are urgently encouraging people to vaccinate against measles.
after newsletter promotion

“In our country we care about rare illnesses and deaths. We care about every child who dies from measles. They get headlines,” he said. “I’d ask you to care about children who are dying or suffering or being injured by vaccine injuries.”
The California warning also follows another recent mass-exposure incident involving Amtrak.

Earlier this week, it was reported that a person infected with measles traveled onboard an Amtrak train from Sedalia, Missouri, to Chicago, Illinois, resulting in more than 250 people being exposed to the virus in Jackson county alone.

This month, it was also revealed that the Trump administration changed how measles deaths are counted during the outbreak. The CDC is now relying on data from the National Center for Health Statistics, which is used to track mortality trends over time. It is unclear why this change was made.

articles.title: Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital after smoke seen rising near Riyadh airport
articles.summary: The King Khalid International Airport incident caused hours of flight disruptions and comes amid an escalating conflict with Houthi rebels in Yemen.

blocks.text: Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen say they carried out drone and missile attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh and energy sites on the country's Red Sea coast.
A column of black smoke was seen rising from what appeared to be fuel tanks near the Saudi capital's international airport on Saturday, hours after air raid alerts were issued.
It was the first time residents had been given an alert and urged to stay indoors since a recent escalation in the conflict with the Houthis.
There has been no official comment from Saudi authorities.

In a statement posted online, Houthi military spokesman Yahya al-Sarea said a "large number of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones" had been used to attack "sensitive sites" in Riyadh and Aramco state oil and gas company facilities in Yanbu on the coast.
He added that the attacks were "in response to the Saudi enemy's criminal attempts" to target the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
Earlier, Sarea had accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out 300 strikes across Yemen during the past week.
The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia.
They have attacked targets inside Saudi Arabia on several occasions in recent months, and said this week that they were responsible for downing a Saudi fighter jet over Yemen.

According to an unconfirmed report from AFP news agency, quoting military sources on both sides of Yemen's civil war, fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces claimed 48 lives on Saturday.
The Houthis said 31 of their fighters had been killed while government sources said their side had lost 17 soldiers, according to the news agency.
On Friday, the International Organization for Migration, a UN body, reported that the number of people displaced as a result of recent fighting had passed 104,796, external.

A number of apparent explosions were heard in Riyadh and major problems were reported at King Khalid International Airport earlier on Saturday, with the tracking website FlightRadar24 reporting delays and cancellations., external
An AFP journalist reported that firefighters could be seen trying to extinguish the flames of a burnt-out fuel tank belonging to Aramco.
The Saudi Civil Defence had sent out phone alerts overnight warning of potential danger in Riyadh and other regions, before issuing an all-clear on Saturday morning.
Residents told AFP on condition of anonymity that they had heard what sounded like a round of explosions echoing through the city after the alerts.
"I heard the alarm, then my windows shook," said a resident of northern Riyadh, 27. "It was definitely scary. I was not expecting this."
The Houthis recently seized control of the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island, a gateway to a key shipping route used by the Gulf state to export to Asia and Europe.
The group said the naval blockade was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen.
Saudi vessels have relied on that stretch of the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

On Friday, investment banking giant JP Morgan said it was struggling to predict how oil prices would be impacted by the war, telling investors in a rare note that "we simply don't know how to model the endgame".

articles.title: Trump announces new 'AI force' amid mounting pressure
articles.summary: Several voices, including from within the AI industry, have been calling for policing the fast-growing technology. Trump has once again called AI warnings "hoaxes" and vowed to "cherish, help" the…

image.caption: Trump claimed that AI is 'the next industrial revolution'Image: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AFP

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has said he is forming an "AI force," as many, including those from within the industry, have recently sounded the alarm about the dangers of the industry continuing to grow unchecked.
In a social media post on Saturday, Trump said he will announce an "AI czar" to lead the force soon.
The US president continued to brush off warnings about AI's dangers as "hoaxes" by the left and Democrats.
What did Trump say about the 'AI force'?
While dismissing warnings about AI, Trump still vowed to be "be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System."

"For this purpose, I am forming the AI Force, much like I did Space Force, which has been a tremendous SUCCESS, in my First Term. To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI 'Czar,'" Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

The US president, who has enjoyed a close relationship with big tech bosses especially during his second term in office, also vowed "not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry," in reference to AI.
"Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows!"
Inside the Broligarchy: Is Big Tech running politics?
He described AI as "the next industrial revolution," predicting it will account for 25% of the US GDP.
"We are leading China, and the rest of the World, and I intend to keep it that way!"
Trump compared the criticism of the unchecked, ultrafast growth of AI to what he called other "hoaxes," listing efforts to impeach him, pro transgender debates and global warming as examples.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran to perform for 1st time since Macklemore dropped from tour, other acts withdrew
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran is set to take the stage in Philadelphia on Saturday night for the first time since facing backlash for rapper Macklemore's removal from his tour for making pro-Palestinian comments on…

image.caption: Ed Sheeran performs in Boston at TD Garden on Dec. 14, 2025. Sheeran is performing in Philadelphia Saturday night for the first time since all his supporting acts withdrew in solidarity with opener Macklemore, who was dropped from the tour after making pro-Palestinian comments onstage. (Paras Griffi

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Ed Sheeran is set to take the stage in Philadelphia on Saturday night for the first time since facing backlash for rapper Macklemore's removal from his tour for making pro-Palestinian comments on stage.
Singer-songwriter hasn't commented publicly since facing backlash for response to Macklemore's removal

All of Sheeran's remaining supporting acts and backing band have quit his tour after Macklemore was ousted earlier this week and Sheeran attributed Macklemore's removal solely to venues and promoters while defending his decision to remain apolitical.
Sheeran has not said anything publicly since losing the artists' support.

However, Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft, who allegedly led efforts to remove Macklemore as Sheeran's opening act, said Wednesday he is now donating $2 million US to "aid in the region" at the singer-songwriter's request.

As of Friday, tickets were still available for Saturday's show, and Sheeran's website did not list any replacement acts. A coalition of pro-Palestinian organizations plans to protest outside the show Saturday afternoon.

Macklemore was dropped from the U.S. leg of the English singer-songwriter's tour after chanting "Free Palestine" and expressing solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza and the Israeli-occupied West Bank during a Sept. 5 show in New Jersey.
How Macklemore's 'Free Palestine' stance derailed Ed Sheeran's entire tour
Sheeran said venues had threatened to pull his upcoming performances if Macklemore was not removed as his opening act because of "how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance."
"Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter's decision, it was not mine. Macklemore's contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me," Sheeran said in his statement.
He added that while he tried to "build a bridge," the venues would not change their minds.
Kraft, who owns the New England Patriots, was one of the people behind the call for Macklemore's removal, Sheeran confirmed.

Kraft, a staunch supporter of Israel, said in a statement shared with CBC News Monday that his stadium would "not provide a platform for hate speech," stating Macklemore spread divisiveness through "selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas."

Macklemore had blamed his removal on Kraft in an Instagram post, claiming the billionaire said the rapper would not be allowed onstage and rallied other stadium owners to threaten to cancel scheduled concerts if he was not taken off the bill. The threats placed Sheeran, his friend, in a difficult position, Macklemore said.
Sheeran takes apolitical stance
Many of Sheeran's supporting acts said they were withdrawing from his tour to stand in solidarity with Palestinians.
In his statement, Sheeran said he was "appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine," and called the suffering on "both sides" a "human tragedy."
But he defended his choice not to express his views on the conflict publicly.
"I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict," he wrote.
"Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn't mean I don't have them, and it doesn't mean I don't care."

items: Ms. Rachel pledges $1M US in Palestinian aid to match Macklemore's donation following Sheeran tour exit
Remaining supporting acts quit Ed Sheeran tour amid backlash over Macklemore ousting

blocks.text: While promoters and venues wield great power over concert tours, experts say an artist of Sheeran's magnitude generally has the final say about what happens concerning the shows.

It remains to be seen how Sheeran will handle the performance at Philadelphia's Lincoln Financial Field given the departure of his opening acts and supporting band. Sheeran has performed much of his Loop Tour concerts solo, but he had been joined for several songs at each stop by the Irish folk band Beoga.
Sheeran's other U.S. openers, Danish band Lukas Graham and Irish singer Aaron Rowe, also annouced they were leaving the tour.
Finneas, Billie Eilish's brother and musical collaborator, was due to tour with Sheeran in South America later this year before he too dropped out earlier this week.

articles.title: Kent hotel fire that forced hundreds to evacuate being treated as suspicious
articles.summary:
No injuries reported after about 280 people taken to safety from the Grand Burstin in Folkestone after blaze

A large fire that broke out overnight at a seaside hotel and forced hundreds of…

blocks.text: Hundreds of people have been evacuated from a hotel in Folkestone after a large fire broke out overnight.
Emergency services were called just after 1am on Saturday to the Grand Burstin hotel in Folkestone, where a fire is believed to have started in the basement, Kent fire and rescue service said.

About 280 people were taken to safety and Folkestone and Hythe district council set up a welfare centre. No injuries relating to the fire have been reported and the cause of the blaze is not yet known.

blocks.caption: Fire damage at the hotel.  Photograph: Andrew Aitchison/In Pictures/Getty Images

blocks.text: Twenty-six fire engines were dispatched to the seafront hotel, the fire service said. According to the Britannia Hotels website, the Grand Burstin overlooks Folkestone’s harbour and has 550 rooms.
Folkestone and Hythe district council posted on X: “A fire is currently ongoing at the Folkestone Grand Burstin hotel.
“We are operating a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park for people being evacuated from the site, where we are providing support to those affected.
“We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety.

“Our advice to residents living nearby is to: close all windows and doors; avoid the area and do not attempt to approach the hotel; follow the instructions of emergency services; keep roads clear to allow emergency vehicles to access the area.”
Kent fire and rescue service said in an update: “Ten fire engines remain at the scene of a fire at the Grand Burstin hotel in The Harbour, Folkestone.
“Crews wearing breathing apparatus have worked hard to bring the fire under control and are now dampening down any remaining hotspots.
“It’s believed the fire started in the basement of the property, but the cause is not yet known.
“Around 280 people evacuated the building, and a welfare centre has been organised by Folkestone and Hythe district council. No fire-related injuries have been reported.”
A spokesperson for Kent police said: “Kent police was called at around 1.20am on Saturday 19 September 2026 to reports of a fire at a hotel on Marine Parade, Folkestone.
“Officers remain in attendance to assist traffic flow while our Kent fire and rescue service colleagues work to tackle the fire.”

articles.title: ‘Holy moly!’: Rare shark visit to Nova Scotia's Bedford Basin inspires shock and awe
articles.summary: It’s been a long time since swimming was encouraged in the Bedford Basin, but that didn’t stop one shark from making a prolonged — and very rare — visit to the water on Friday night.

image.caption: A basking shark made a rare appearance in the Bedford Basin on Friday evening. (Submitted by Lisa McCloskey)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia
It’s been a long time since swimming was encouraged in the Bedford Basin, but that didn’t stop one shark from making a prolonged — and very rare — visit to the water on Friday night.
Shark expert says basking sharks 'completely harmless'
It’s been a long time since swimming was encouraged in the Bedford Basin, but that didn’t stop one shark from making a rare and lengthy visit on Friday night.
"I have never seen a shark in the Bedford Basin before. That was a first," said Bedford resident John Calder.
Calder had nearly finished his commute home from work when he came across a crowd standing on the Shore Drive Bridge, which overlooks the basin where it meets the Sackville River.

“I got out of my car to see what was happening and lo and behold, there was two giant shark fins that were protruding from the water,” Calder said Saturday. “Right away, I said: 'Holy moly! That's a shark.'"
According to marine biologist and shark researcher Neil Hammerschlag, who reviewed multiple videos of the shark shared on social media, “it’s clearly a basking shark.”

“They pose no risk to humans, they eat little plankton, and they’re called basking sharks because they often spend time near the surface where they look like they’re basking in the sun,” said Hammerschlag, president of Atlantic Shark Expeditions.
The shark's habit of floating near the surface, combined with the fact that it is the second-largest fish in the world, made it easy to spot once it entered the basin.
However, finding one in such a busy waterway — surrounded by dozens of sailboats and densely populated shores — is highly unusual.
“I think this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to see an animal this large so close to shore,” Hammerschlag said.
Shark spent hours in basin
While Calder watched the shark for only 15 minutes before it swam away, he described it as a moment where time stood still.
“You go about your day, and then all of a sudden there’s a shark, and it’s like everything stops, nothing else is important and you’re just watching mother nature,” he said.
Around 7:30 p.m., Calder's wife, Lisa McCloskey, and his 14-year-old stepdaughter, Audrey Hill, spotted the shark near a dock at the Bedford Basin Yacht Club.

“It seemed kind of surreal,” McCloskey said. “We could almost see our house in the distance, and then we’re watching this massive shark come out of the water and it came near us and almost rolled over so we saw its whole body as well ... it was magical.”
For nearly two hours, a growing crowd watched as the shark surfaced and submerged.

“There were probably like 30 or 40 of us, and people were hugging each other when they saw the shark,” McCloskey said. “It really felt like a community event. Everyone was chatting and it was really lovely.”
Hammerschlag said it remains unclear why the shark ventured into the basin. Basking sharks are far more common in open, plankton-rich waters like the Bay of Fundy.
The shark may have been unwell or disoriented, Hammerschlag said, but “unless it washes up on shore,” there's no way to know for sure.
“Either way, it’s a remarkable encounter, and this is a beautiful animal, completely harmless to people, and whoever had the opportunity to see it should consider themselves lucky.”

articles.title: Canada's top general loses election to become head of key NATO Military Committee
articles.summary: Despite a push from the federal government, Canada's chief of the defence staff has lost a vote to be the next chair of the NATO Military Committee, the alliance's top military authority and a key…

image.caption: Gen. Jennie Carignan at a news conference in Victoria on Sept. 2. The chief of the defence staff has lost her bid to become the next chair of the NATO Military Committee. (Chad Hipolito/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

Despite a push from the federal government, Canada's chief of the defence staff has lost a vote to be the next chair of the NATO Military Committee, the alliance's top military authority and a key advisory body for its political leaders.
Gen. Jennie Carignan's German counterpart named chair of influential advisory body
· CBC News
· Posted: Sep 19, 2026 12:53 PM EDT | Last Updated: 7 minutes ago

Gen. Jennie Carignan and her German counterpart, Gen. Carsten Breuer, were vying for the position. Top military commanders from NATO's 32 members ultimately decided on Saturday to go with Breuer in a secret ballot election.
The news was announced on social media by the current chair, Italian Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, who congratulated Breuer on his election.
"Your operational judgement, your deep familiarity with this alliance and your leadership of the German Armed Forces will serve NATO well," Dragone said.

A Canadian has not held this position in almost two decades — the last being retired general Ray Henault between 2005 and 2008. Had she won, Carignan would have been the first woman to lead the Military Committee in the 77-year history of the alliance.
Statement on the election of a new chair of the NATO Military Committee: pic.twitter.com/8lMUTVhDQ5—CDS_Canada_CEMD

In a statement posted to social media, Carignan congratulated Breuer and said, "it was an honour to stand as a candidate and to engage with my fellow Allied Chiefs of Defence throughout this process."

"There is important work ahead for our Alliance, and I know General Breuer will bring strong leadership to his new role. I deeply value the close relationship we have built and look forward to continuing to work together on our NATO initiatives," Carignan added.
On Friday, Defence Minister David McGuinty said Carignan deserved the job because she's worked very hard and has "enormous credibility."

items: EU chief says she wants Canada to become the bloc's 1st associate member

blocks.text: "She has reached out to her counterparts in all NATO alliance member countries," McGuinty said following a Liberal caucus meeting in Ottawa. "It would be historical and groundbreaking, the first woman chief of defence to chair such a committee."
CBC News has contacted McGuinty's office for comment on the election result.
Potential U.S. obstacles to Carignan appointment

Experts who previously spoke to CBC News said a potential roadblock to Carignan winning would be U.S. President Donald Trump — particularly after Prime Minister Mark Carney formally unveiled his intent to strengthen Canada's ties to the European Union.

"Trump is not going to let a Canadian or a woman be the head of the military committee, if anybody around him has paid attention to it," said Steven Saideman, a defence expert at Carleton University who's written extensively about NATO.

items: Canada's top general is up for a senior NATO post. Will Trump get in her way?

blocks.text: The elected chair, Breuer, is a 61-year-old army officer who earned the nickname "the chancellor's general" after then-German chancellor Olaf Scholz picked him to lead a crisis committee that helped manage the country's response to the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021 and 2022.
He joined the Bundeswehr in an air defence unit in 1984, and later attended the U.S. general staff college in Fort Leavenworth, Kan., as well as German general staff training in Hamburg.
In 2014, Breuer served with NATO's International Security Assistance Force in the Afghan capital Kabul.
Dragone said on social media that Breuer will take office in July 2027.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy ex-husband says ‘I think I did the best I could’
articles.summary:
Patrick Clancy and wife Rachel Danis to speak publicly on 60 Minutes on Sunday about Massachusetts murder trial

Patrick Clancy and his wife Rachel Danis are set to describe their experiences…

blocks.text: Patrick Clancy and his wife Rachel Danis are set to describe their experiences of the Massachusetts triple-murder trial of his former wife Lindsay Clancy, with Clancy telling 60 Minutes: “I live with it every day, but I think I did the best I could.”
The couple will on Sunday night make their first public comments on the case. CBS has been trailing excerpts of the broadcast.

The interviews with the pair marks a second significant media “get” for 60 Minutes since it came under new leadership earlier this year. Last week, it secured an interview with a pilot who was rescued by special forces after being shot down over Iran.

The Clancy interviews come as Massachusetts prosecutors are set to decide later this month whether to retry Lindsay Clancy over the killings of the couple’s three children – Cora, five; Dawson, three; and Callan, eight months old – in January 2023. A hearing is slated for 29 September at Plymouth superior court.

A trial over the summer riveted public attention and ended in a mistrial when a single juror rejected the Clancy’s defense position that she had carried out the killings because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis that meant she could not be found criminally responsible for her actions.

The trial shed light on the little-understood mental health condition, and the resulting mistrial sharply divided public opinion. The single holdout juror, Michael Desronvil, came forward last week to say he thought enough physical evidence and key witness testimony presented at trial proved Clancy “knew exactly what she was doing and planned [it]”.

Patrick Clancy, who testified in the prosecution phase of the trial but has supported his former wife, has been subject to intense speculation outside the courtroom from online content creators and conspiracists.
Earlier this month, an attorney for Clancy threatened legal “consequences” over what he called a “relentless, escalating and destructive defamation campaign” targeting his client.

“Enough is enough – this spread of blatant and baseless falsehoods must stop,” attorney Howard Cooper said. “Those responsible should understand that there will be consequences, and every appropriate measure will be pursued to hold them accountable, including legally.”
According to excerpts of the 60 Minutes interviews released ahead of airtime, Patrick Clancy talks about his grief, his memories of his children, and conspiracy theories.

Clancy tells correspondent Ross Douthat he still talks to his kids “all the time” and asked them for help. Asked if they do, Clancy responds: “I like to believe they do. It’s a way I stay connected to them.”

Clancy, who discovered his three children after finding his injured wife lying in snow below a second floor window and is now paralyzed from the waist down, also told the news program: “I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time, and I live with the outcome. I live with it every day, but I think I did the best I could.”

The Clancys repeatedly sought psychiatric and mental care for the young mother in the months before the incident, and have since filed a civil lawsuit alleging negligence and over-prescription of medications on the the part of two health professionals and healthcare providers.
In the released interview excerpts, Danis, 37, discusses how she met Patrick, their marriage, and defends her husband against the theories that have appeared online.

“I don’t understand how the story’s been so twisted, but I would hope people know that Pat is, as I said before, the most selfless father and supportive partner,” Danis, an infertility specialist, tells the program.

The couple met while jogging and Patrick moved to New York and married earlier this year, she says. “I was just a girl that met a guy running in Central Park on a really cold Saturday, and I don’t think there’s anything wrong with that.”

articles.title: German-Russian relations at freezing point
articles.summary: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine destroyed the once-close relationship between Moscow and Berlin. Yet the far-right AfD is calling for a normalization of relations.

image.caption: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (left) has described Russian President Vladimir Putin as "perhaps the worst war criminal of our time"Image: picture alliance

blocks.text: For many years, Germany and Russia had a perfect partnership.

Russia supplied cheap energy, which helped German industry succeed in exporting its goods worldwide. This partnership began in the early 2000s. On the German side was Chancellor Gerhard Schröder from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), followed later by Chancellor Angela Merkel of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Their counterpart was Vladimir Putin.

Even when Russia annexed the Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea in 2014, business continued as usual. It was then that the agreement to build Nord Stream 2, a direct gas pipeline between Russia and Germany designed to bypass Ukraine was signed. At the time, other European countries and the US warned that the pipeline would provide Russia with powerful leverage.

The warnings proved to be correct. On February 24, 2022, Russian tanks rolled into Ukraine. German hopes for a stable European order, the democratization of Russia, and the continuation of its lucrative business model were shattered.
Hundreds of fake posts target German elections
How could so many German politicians be so wrong?

"Shortly before the invasion, the widespread view was that there were no rational grounds for an attack on Ukraine, because the economic, military, and political costs to Russia of starting a war would be far too high," Russia expert Mario Baumann of the German Council on Foreign Relations told DW. "People [in Germany] had projected their own rationality onto Russia. They underestimated the regime's imperialist and revisionist ambitions."

After that, nothing in the bilateral relationship was ever the same again. Chancellor Olaf Scholz(SPD) spoke of a Zeitenwende (epochal shift) in foreign and security policy, in the days after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine began.

Since then, the German armed forces have expanded. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said the following year, "We must become capable of waging war," a statement that critics still say was an escalation of tensions.

Germany ended its decades-long energy dependence on Russia and shut down Nord Stream 2. In September 2022, the pipeline was blown up. The Federal Prosecutor's Office suspects a Ukrainian group was responsible.
A series of EU sanctions have long since reduced Russian-German trade relations to a minimum. Government cooperation in culture, science, and education has also practically ceased to exist.
A new low point
While the German government under Scholz initially hesitated to take dramatic steps on military aid to Ukraine, Friedrich Merz, then the leader of the opposition, stepped up his rhetoric.

"Ukraine must win the war. Russia must lose the war," he said in 2024 as leader of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group in parliament. In 2025, as chancellor, he then spoke of Russia's "economic exhaustion," which the West must "help bring about." But that has yet to materialize. To this day, Russia has shown no serious willingness to compromise.
Why Putin turned to ex‑German chancellor as a peace broker

Meanwhile, Germany is feeling the consequences of its military support for Ukraine. The German government has long suspected Russia of being behind cyberattacks on government agencies and critical infrastructure.

So when an armed drone was discovered and defused in August 2026 at Leipzig Airport close to Ukrainian transport aircraft — which transport a large portion of the military aid to Ukraine — the government was certain: For the first time, it publicly blamed the Kremlin.

A Russian cultural center in Berlin and the Russian consulate in Bonn were closed, which the German government said were being used as espionage centers. Moscow responded by closing the Goethe Institutes and the German consulate in St. Petersburg.

Putin has denied Russian responsibility for the Leipzig incident, calling it a "serious mistake" to blame Moscow, while Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov even described the accusations as the "beginning of a real war." But Baumann says: "We shouldn't give in to the fears being stoked, because they are part of Russia's strategy to weaken Germany and Europe."
AfD wants to resume relations with Russia

The German government is also facing domestic pressure as the far-right Alternative for Germany(AfD) has made gains in regional elections and is rising in the national polls. The AfD would prefer to end support for Ukraine and normalize relations with Russia, including deals on oil and gas. High fuel prices in Germany have only made the issue more explosive.

"German support for Ukraine worries many people," said Sven Leunig, political scientist at the University of Jena in Thuringia, following the election in the neighboring state of Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD won the September 6 election by a landslide. However, he noted, "it is less a fundamental rejection of the support itself than a reaction born of fear. People want to 'stay out' of the conflict so as not to be drawn into it more deeply themselves."

In the latest ARD Deutschlandtrend survey, 42% of respondents believe military aid to Ukraine has gone too far. "If public support weakens over the long term, the government will eventually have to respond," says Leunig.
Carry on or change course?

So far, the German government is sticking to its course, as Merz made clear once again following the AfD's election victory. But opinions on how to deal with Russia and the war in Ukraine differ not only among politicians but also among political scientists and experts.

Johannes Varwick of Halle University in Saxony-Anhalt believes it is long past time for a change of course: "German and European policy toward Ukraine resembles a mix of platitudes and wishful thinking," Varwick told DW. "It is high time for a course correction, and Germany should exert pressure on Ukraine to move closer to the latest American proposals, which aim for a compromise and could thus possibly bring about a political solution."

Baumann, on the other hand, argues: "Supporting Ukraine remains the best investment for safeguarding German and European interests. The government has recognized this and should stick to this course and continue to communicate it as such." However, it is important that Berlin act in concert with its European partners.

The war in Ukraine has now lasted longer than World War I. And there is no end in sight. Hopes that Russian-German relations will return to the way they used to be seem illusory for the foreseeable future.
This article was translated from German.

articles.title: Elderly man allegedly beaten to death in Virginia Walmart by parents of employee
articles.summary:
Bert Atienza and teen worker reportedly exchanged words before parents showed up and allegedly attacked shopper

A 77-year-old

blocks.text: A 77-year-old Walmart shopper died after he was allegedly attacked inside a Virginia store by the parents of a teenage employee he had confronted over a shopping cart incident involving his wife, according to US media reports.
Bert Atienza died from blunt head trauma on 8 June, one day after the attack at the Walmart in Norfolk, Virginia, WTKR reported on Monday. The shocking incident was captured on surveillance video.
Police responded to the store at about 3.20pm on 7 June after receiving a report of an assault.
Atienza’s wife, Josephine, was left on the floor holding her injured husband in her lap after the attack, according to video from the scene.

“My husband was still able to speak, he said, ‘Help me get up,’ but I told him, ‘No, you’re bleeding. Your mouth is bleeding. Ambulance is coming,” Josephine said. “I look at him again. He has no more consciousness.”
Atienza was found unresponsive and taken to a hospital, where he died from his injuries the following day. Medical officials ruled his death a homicide caused by blunt force trauma.
The confrontation began while Atienza and his wife of 42 years were grocery-shopping after spending the morning at church.

Josephine said a 17-year-old Walmart employee came quickly down the aisle where the couple was shopping and nearly struck her with a shopping cart. Atienza and the unidentified worker exchanged words before the employee allegedly threw a can toward the couple as they walked away, Josephine told WTKR.

The teen then reportedly called her parents, Travis White and Erika Mitchell, who began looking for the couple inside the store minutes later. The store surveillance video shows what appears to be Atienza looking at items on a shelf when White and Mitchell approached and attacked him while their daughter watched.

The elderly shopper was allegedly shoved from behind, grabbed and punched as people nearby walked away. He was then pushed into a shelving unit and fell to the floor, where one of the suspects allegedly kicked him.
White, 44, and Mitchell, 42, were arrested days later and are being held without bond in the Norfolk jail.

Their teenage daughter was also charged with assault and battery, aggravated malicious wounding, and conspiracy to commit a felony, according to WAVY. She is being held at the Norfolk juvenile detention center. Authorities have not released her name because she is a minor.

articles.title: Palace orders prompt processing of MAIFIP claims
articles.summary: Malacañang has ordered the Department of Health to work closely with its regional directors and hospitals to ensure the timely processing of legitimate claims under a program designed to…

blocks.text: September 20, 2026 | 12:00am
Patients infected with dengue rest at a hospital ward in Manila on Feb. 19, 2025.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang has ordered the Department of Health (DOH) to work closely with its regional directors and hospitals to ensure the timely processing of legitimate claims under a program designed to assist patients facing financial difficulties.

The office of Executive Secretary Ralph Recto said the timely processing of claims, under the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) program, would help health care facilities sustain strong operations and ensure uninterrupted care to patients from vulnerable and low-income communities.

“Let us continue coordinating with the regional directors, verify the accounts payable and process the valid claims promptly. These funds are available to support our patients and our partner hospitals,” Recto said in a statement issued yesterday.
Funds from MAIFIP will be used to support valid claims for essential health care services like hospitalization, medicine, emergency treatment, professional fees and other necessary medical expenses.
The Department of Budget and Management recently released P27.4 billion to the DOH for the continued implementation of the program under this year’s national budget.
The bulk of the allocation – P19.145 billion – will be given to DOH health development centers to provide medical assistance through regional networks and partner health care facilities nationwide.

DOH hospitals in Metro Manila will receive P4.353 billion, while the Lung Center of the Philippines, National Kidney and Transplant Institute, Philippine Children’s Medical Center and Philippine Heart Center will be given P2.910 billion.
The administration will provide P950 million to the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital and P52 million to drug abuse treatment and rehabilitation centers.

articles.title: Romualdez camp: Ex-speaker not a corruption mastermind
articles.summary: The camp of former Speaker Martin Romualdez insisted that he is not the so-called mastermind of the flood control corruption scheme, saying he only did his part to get the budget approved and has no…

blocks.text: September 20, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The camp of former Speaker Martin Romualdez insisted that he is not the so-called mastermind of the flood control corruption scheme, saying he only did his part to get the budget approved and has no control over individual projects.

Romualdez’s counsel, Atty. Jose Roy III, said the Leyte lawmaker is confounded on being tagged as a central figure in the flood control kickback scheme, considering that the corruption scandal involves individual projects, over which he has no control.
Roy explained that Romualdez was only involved in the budget process and had no control over individual projects.

“As far as he knows, he was doing his share to get the budget approved. Now he’s being made to account for all those acts. He can’t understand why this is happening, when in fact, the same functions are performed on the Senate level,” he said.
Roy insisted that the flood control scheme worked on a “per-project basis” and it’s not possible for a mastermind behind it.

“It’s like we pass the budget and we take a whole chunk and this is ours. I don’t think that’s possible,” he said, explaining that after the budget is passed, it goes back to the executive, which implements the individual projects.
Moreover, Roy said it is “unthinkable” to put all this all on one person and say he handled all the anomalous projects, pointing out that each district has its own favored contracts.
“No matter how you look at it, those issues involving contracts, document tampering, questionable bids and ghost projects – those things happen at the lower level, not at the budget stage,” he said.
